title: Load balancing inside and outside the cluster

videos.script: Lesson 15 said kube-proxy picks a pod for each connection. This lesson opens the rules it writes, and counts what they do. {{rules}} Inside the cluster the choice is random, and the rules say so in plain numbers: one chance in three, then one in two, then the last pod. Three hundred requests show how even random is. {{random}} Then you will pin a client to one pod, and see why that is rarely what you want. {{pin}} Outside the cluster there is a second decision. A request can arrive at a node with no pod, and be passed on, losing the caller's address on the way. Or the node can refuse it, and keep the address. {{outside}} One field chooses, and each choice has a price. {{price}}
